name: Correctarr
description: Correctarr finds and fixes the problems Radarr, Sonarr, SABnzbd and Prowlarr leave lying around because nobody is looking: wrongly matched releases, downloads that break today's profile rules, stuck imports, files that cannot be matched to a title, and leftover debris in the download folders. It works three ways at once: in real time through webhooks, on a short schedule for the queue, and on a full pass for the library and the indexers. 33 rules, and you decide per rule what happens when one of them finds something — from reporting it to blocklisting, importing, searching again or deleting. Conditions such as "wait six hours first" or "nothing over 20 GB" narrow that down further. It also builds quality profiles. Six questions — which resolutions, how good the sound, which languages and whether they are compulsory, which codec, what size, may a file be replaced — and it writes the profile and every custom format behind it into Radarr and Sonarr, showing you the whole plan first. Those profiles cannot cause a download loop: they never upgrade on score, only up the resolution ladder, which is finite. A dry run switch stops every change at once, and it is ON after a fresh install: everything is found and reported, nothing is touched, until you have seen the findings and turned it off yourself. Guiding principle: when in doubt, do nothing. A rule that is not sure only reports. Better one finding left alone than one good file thrown away. SETUP Open the web interface after the first start and create an account (username and password). A setup assistant then walks you through connecting Radarr, Sonarr, SABnzbd and Prowlarr, testing each one as you go, and checking the paths. IMPORTANT, ABOUT THE PATHS The paths have to be the same inside this container as the ones Radarr and Sonarr see. Mount the download folders exactly the way you mounted them there. The overview page tells you whether that worked. LANGUAGES The interface is available in English and German and follows your browser by default. SECURITY The interface has its own login. If you already run Authelia, Authentik or basic auth in a reverse proxy in front of it, you can turn it off with AUTH=off. Without one of the two, the port does not belong on the open internet.

paths.name: Configuration and history
paths.description: Holds the database, the settings, the services and the history. This directory survives a container update and must not be deleted.

paths.name: Finished downloads
paths.description: The folder SABnzbd puts finished downloads in. This MUST be the same one Radarr and Sonarr see, otherwise Correctarr cannot find the files. Write access is needed for cleanup.

paths.name: Incomplete downloads
paths.description: The working folder of SABnzbd. Leave empty if there is no separate one.

paths.name: Movies
paths.description: The movie library. Read only. Optional — without it a few details are missing from the overview.

paths.name: Series
paths.description: The series library. Read only. Optional.

ports.name: Web interface
ports.description: The port the interface is reachable on in a browser. If it clashes with something, put a different number here; the WebUI button follows automatically.

variables.name: Authentication
variables.description: on = built-in login with username and password (recommended). off = no login; only sensible when Authelia, Authentik or basic auth in a reverse proxy already handles it.

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Used for timestamps and scheduling, for example Europe/Berlin or America/New_York.

variables.name: Sub path behind a reverse proxy
variables.description: Only needed when the interface runs under a sub path such as /correctarr. Leave empty when it has its own hostname or is reached directly on the port.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User id the service runs as. On Unraid 99 (nobody) is correct.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group id. On Unraid 100 (users) is correct.

variables.name: UMASK
variables.description: Permission mask for newly created files.

variables.name: Log level
variables.description: INFO in normal operation. DEBUG for troubleshooting only, it gets very chatty. Credentials are redacted either way.

variables.name: Radarr address (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only: adopts the service automatically. Everything is managed in the interface afterwards and this variable is ignored.

variables.name: Radarr API key (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only. Found in Radarr under Settings, General.

variables.name: Sonarr address (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only.

variables.name: Sonarr API key (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only.

variables.name: SABnzbd address (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only. Without SABnzbd nothing is classified as debris and nothing is deleted.

variables.name: SABnzbd API key (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only.

variables.name: Prowlarr address (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only. Optional — without Prowlarr there is no indexer rating.

variables.name: Prowlarr API key (first run only)
variables.description: For the very first start only.
